correctness.rationale: For each alpha>0, the normalized harmonic basis follows from Gamma radial moments. For each a in circle L2, its finite-mode products are L2 and Pythagoras yields the exact nonnegative sum |a_m|^2 S_N(m). Gamma midpoint convexity gives 1-W^2=m^2/(2 alpha |j|)+O(j^-2) at both tails. A universal trigamma estimate bounds S_N(m)/logN by C_alpha m^2. Dominated convergence for a in H1 and Fatou for a not in H1 prove the complete extended-value statement. For bounded unimodular a, the Toeplitz defect is exactly the Hankel squared norm. Gaussian m=2 gives an exact harmonic-number check; 1907 finite assertions passed but do not substitute for infinite proof.

value.rationale: The object is the intrinsic loss of harmonicity under angular multiplication on generalized Fock spaces. The theorem identifies its sharp asymptotic divergence coefficient as the circle Dirichlet energy and provides an exact necessary-and-sufficient Sobolev regularity boundary for every angular L2 input. Its explicit coefficient 1/alpha is sensitive to the radial Fock geometry, while the qualitative H1 boundary remains universal. This is a structural trace/regularity law rather than a finite numerical lookup or a substitution exercise.
